newsitem.title: USA: Grand Coulee hydropower output seen down until Mon.
newsitem.headline: Grand Coulee hydropower output seen down until Mon.

text.p: Slower discharge from the Grand Coulee hydropower dam, the uppermost U.S. project on the Columbia River, will mean less power generation through Monday, a spokeswoman for the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Tuesday.
She noted Canadian projects have curtailed flows in order to re-fill reservoirs at the same time U.S. flows have dropped amid warmer summer weather.
Grand Coulee has a rated power capacity of 6,150 megawatts (MW).
U.S. dams are also re-filling ahead of end-July targets related to upstream migration of endangered fish species.
For the next several days, flows from Grand Coulee are expected to drop by an average 20,000 to 30,000 cubic feet per second (cfs) from a current rate of around 140,000 cfs, the spokeswoman said.
But discharge is scheduled to rise starting Monday when extra water from Canada moves into the U.S. system, she said.
BPA noted it will be able "shape" flows from Coulee, running more water during daytime peak demand hours and less during off-peak hours.
A 600 MW power turbine at Grand Coulee is scheduled to return to service Wednesday after being shut since February for maintenance, but BPA said power generation will not be affected.
"Until Monday we won't have enough water to run near capacity," the BPA spokeswoman said.
